scope_note: cs.CV/cs.RO /new listings for 2026-07-31 were parsed with repository scripts. The parser found 131 non-replacement cs.CV rows and 32 non-replacement cs.RO rows; after deduplication, 157 papers remained and 131 were classified as ROI. Tier A uses official arXiv HTML for EgoGenesis, ACE-Data-0, Counterfactual Action Sensitivity Coverage, RedFlow, TacWAM, World Action Planner, ODEWorld, LabEvolver, and rest-state articulated reconstruction.
executive_thesis: The July 31 batch turns the week into a clear research decision: robot learning is moving from more demonstrations and better-looking futures toward counterfactual coverage, action-sensitive world models, and runtime correction. Counterfactual Action Sensitivity Coverage asks which new examples actually repair a trained policy's nuisance-induced action drift. RedFlow then converts failed rollouts into action-level corrective targets instead of discarding them. EgoGenesis, TacWAM, World Action Planner, and ODEWorld each make a different state variable explicit: anchored 3D memory, mechanics-aware tactile futures, pose-image world-model rollouts, or continuous physical-time flow. ACE-Data-0 and LabEvolver broaden the same lesson to data and agents: synchronized human interaction streams and evolved wet-lab experience are assets only when the state they preserve is typed. APRL should prioritize a counterfactual action-sensitivity and world-action ledger over another generic demo-scaling run.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Demo value is measured by action drift coverage
decision_cards.body: The counterfactual coverage paper and RedFlow both reject undifferentiated data growth. A new sample matters when it changes the action under a nuisance or supplies a corrective target for a failed step.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: World-action models need the missing physical channel
decision_cards.body: EgoGenesis adds anchored 3D memory, TacWAM adds tactile mechanics, ODEWorld adds physical-time flow, and World Action Planner uses pose-image rollouts for search. Each paper names the state absent from pixel futures.

decision_cards.label: Decision
decision_cards.title: Experience becomes reusable only after safety and state are summarized
decision_cards.body: LabEvolver turns completed wet-lab traces into skills, strategies, and safety memories; ACE-Data-0 synchronizes perception, pose, object, audio, and contact. The asset is not the raw trace but the reusable state abstraction.

papers.title: EgoGenesis: Egocentric World-Action Modeling with Online Anchored Projective Memory and Action-3D RoPE
papers.fit: egocentric world-action modeling - anchored 3D memory - action geometry
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Egocentric video generation can look plausible while camera motion, gripper trajectory, and object interaction drift away from the intended action.
papers.friction: Embodied data is scarce, but synthetic egocentric video is not useful for robot learning unless it preserves scene anchors and action geometry.
papers.hidden_premise: A generated manipulation video should remember the first-frame 3D scene and encode end-effector motion in camera-aware coordinates.
papers.conceptual_move: EgoGenesis adds Online Anchored Projective Memory and Action-3D RoPE to a pretrained video prior for controllable egocentric interaction generation.
papers.mechanism: OAPM stores anchored and recent 3D scene slots, while A3D-RoPE injects metric action geometry into skeleton-to-video cross-attention during autoregressive generation.

evidence.claim: The paper diagnoses uncontrolled camera motion and gripper trajectory drift in existing egocentric video generators.
The architecture shows OAPM maintaining anchored and recent 3D scene slots and A3D-RoPE injecting action geometry.
Generation quality is compared on held-out trajectories under identical scene and action conditioning.
The HTML lists geometric drift, spatial influence, scene-memory ablation, and downstream WAM generalization.

papers.falsification: If generated trajectories improve video metrics but not downstream real-robot WAM generalization, anchored memory is not preserving the right control variable.
papers.adversarial: A3D action geometry can still be a clean skeleton prior that hides contact ambiguity, force, and gripper-object slip.
papers.thinking_tool: Treat generated egocentric data as valid only when it preserves anchor state, end-effector geometry, and downstream policy effect.
papers.transfer_boundary: Transfers to visuomotor manipulation data augmentation; less direct for contact-rich tasks without tactile or force state.

papers.title: ACE-Data-0: Human-Centric Ambient Capture as Embodied Data Engine
papers.fit: ambient embodied data - synchronized multimodal capture - human interaction state
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Embodied datasets often split egocentric video, exocentric views, body pose, hand-object motion, audio, and tactile contact into separate corpora.
papers.friction: Robot imitation and world models need the full perception-action loop, but home-scale activity and close hand-object contact require different sensor geometry.
papers.hidden_premise: A data engine can be valuable if it captures every important interaction signal, synchronizes it, and keeps it in a common spatial frame.
papers.conceptual_move: ACE turns real homes into calibrated recording studios at table and room scales, releasing synchronized multimodal interaction streams.
papers.mechanism: The system captures egocentric and exocentric video, body and hand pose, object state, sound, and contact annotations across complementary spatial scales.

evidence.claim: ACE is presented as a capture system that transforms real home environments into table-scale and room-scale recording studios.
The architecture separates close manipulation capture from whole-room motion capture while keeping signals registered.
The paper contrasts ACE with egocentric datasets and motion-capture HOI datasets that fragment modalities.
The HTML states that current methods expose gaps under contact, occlusion, egomotion, and long horizons.

papers.falsification: If synchronized ambient capture does not improve policy learning or world-model prediction compared with cheaper partial sensors, the data engine is over-specified.
papers.adversarial: Rich capture can create a private-studio bias: the hardest household deployment variation may sit outside the calibrated homes.
papers.thinking_tool: Audit data sources by preserved state variables and synchronization error, not just hours or number of demonstrations.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for household and dexterous interaction data; field robots and laboratories need domain-specific sensors and safety labels.

papers.title: It's Not Just More Demos: Counterfactual Action Sensitivity Coverage for Data-Efficient Robust Robot Imitation
papers.fit: counterfactual data selection - action drift - robust imitation repair
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Imitation policies are often repaired by collecting more diverse demonstrations without knowing which examples address the trained policy's brittle action boundary.
papers.friction: Lighting, distractors, color, or local support changes can preserve the task but still push the policy action away from the expert action.
papers.hidden_premise: The useful new data is the data that covers action drift under task-preserving nuisances.
papers.conceptual_move: CFNBC generates paired clean and nuisance observations, measures action drift, and selects counterfactual examples for targeted robustness repair.
papers.mechanism: A nominal policy is probed with counterfactual nuisance grids; high-response examples define repair candidates for fine-tuning under a low data budget.

evidence.claim: The paper defines representative task-preserving nuisance conditions including appearance, lighting, distractor, local support, and multi-factor combinations.
The official HTML reports response-guided repair improving all-nuisance success by +0.66 in cube transfer and +0.44 in cube stacking at matched low budgets.
The method separates task-preserving counterfactuals, action drift, response-guided repair selection, and repair fine-tuning.
The paper includes narrow repair and held-out nuisance generalization analyses.

papers.falsification: If action-drift-selected examples do not transfer to held-out nuisance families, the method is selecting visible variation rather than causal brittleness.
papers.adversarial: Counterfactual rendering can preserve the expert action by construction while missing real-world nuisance physics or perception artifacts.
papers.thinking_tool: Before adding demonstrations, ask which nuisance changes the policy action while preserving the expert action.
papers.transfer_boundary: Best for visuomotor imitation with controllable nuisance generation; harder for tasks where the nuisance changes the valid expert action.

papers.title: RedFlow: Redirect Failure into Action-Level Corrections for Flow-matching VLA Policy
papers.fit: failure-to-correction learning - flow-matching VLA - offline RL
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Offline improvement often imitates success or learns trajectory-level preferences, leaving failed rollouts underused as action-level supervision.
papers.friction: A failed rollout contains diagnostic information, but it must be localized to the action that caused progress to break.
papers.hidden_premise: Failure can be redirected if a similar successful context supplies a corrective action target.
papers.conceptual_move: RedFlow finds failure-inducing actions and maps them to corrective targets from successful experiences in matched contexts.
papers.mechanism: Context-aware corrective matching estimates task progress, clusters similar execution contexts, and trains an adaptive redirection objective for flow-matching policies.

evidence.claim: The paper contrasts trajectory-level failure learning with RedFlow's action-level corrective guidance.
The pipeline includes data collection, context-aware corrective matching, and adaptive redirection.
LIBERO average success is reported as 56.2 for the base policy, 62.3 for AWR, 59.7 for DPO, and 68.2 for RedFlow.
The paper includes ablation, sample efficiency, real-robot results, and qualitative recovery analysis.

papers.falsification: If matched successful contexts are semantically similar but dynamically different, corrective targets can push the policy toward a plausible but wrong action.
papers.adversarial: Progress estimators can encode benchmark-specific task phases; failure localization needs inspection on natural real-robot failures.
papers.thinking_tool: Store failed action, progress estimate, matched successful context, corrective target, and post-repair action error.
papers.transfer_boundary: Transfers to flow-matching VLA policies with rollout buffers; less direct for policies without comparable latent or action-space geometry.

papers.title: TacWAM: Anchor-Guided World Action Model with Mechanics-Aware Tactile Prediction
papers.fit: tactile world-action model - contact-rich manipulation - mechanics-aware futures
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: World Action Models mostly predict visual futures, which can omit force, deformation, shear, and slip during contact.
papers.friction: Tactile futures are useful only if they carry physical information without becoming privileged future cues for action generation.
papers.hidden_premise: A WAM can predict tactile state while keeping action tokens restricted to deployment-available context.
papers.conceptual_move: TacWAM builds mechanics-aware tactile prediction and anchor-guided tri-modal attention into a WAM.
papers.mechanism: A tactile encoder fuses appearance, force fields, and deformation flow; AGT attention separates observable anchors, prediction targets, and action tokens.

evidence.claim: The overview shows joint prediction of visual futures, tactile futures, and action chunks from deployment-available context.
AGT visibility rules prevent action tokens from reading future visual or tactile prediction tokens.
Real-world tasks cover fragile grasping, contact localization, sustained contact, and in-hand manipulation.
TacWAM reports 75.0% average success across four contact-rich tasks versus lower visual/tactile baselines.

papers.falsification: If tactile prediction quality does not correlate with contact success, the tactile future is auxiliary supervision rather than a planning state.
papers.adversarial: Tactile sensors can make the benchmark hardware-specific; transfer to different grippers or materials must be tested.
papers.thinking_tool: Evaluate WAMs by which physical channels they preserve: vision, force, deformation, slip, and action feasibility.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for contact-rich manipulation with tactile sensing; weaker for long-range navigation or tasks without tactile feedback.

papers.title: World Action Planner: Generalizable Decision-Making with Action-Conditioned World Models
papers.fit: world-model planning - pose-image conditioning - compositional generalization
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: End-to-end imitation policies can fit training tasks but struggle to compose new layouts and tasks at test time.
papers.friction: Planning over imagined futures needs a world model that generalizes to new actions and embodiments, not only known low-dimensional action vectors.
papers.hidden_premise: Rendering future robot joint positions as pose images can provide an action-conditioned world model that is easier to search over.
papers.conceptual_move: World Action Planner combines VLM reasoning with pose-image conditioned world-model rollouts for iterative plan refinement.
papers.mechanism: The system proposes an initial plan, renders action-conditioned pose images, imagines future rollouts, then optimizes and searches over plan candidates.

evidence.claim: The planner reasons about and refines action plans through world-model imagination for novel scenarios.
The world model conditions on future robot joint positions rendered as pose skeleton images.
The official HTML reports average improvements of 11.4% in-distribution and 16.8% in generalization settings for single-embodiment world modeling.
Cross-embodiment modeling is evaluated across fixed arm, mobile Panda, bi-manual gripper, and dexterous-hand settings.

papers.falsification: If search succeeds only when the world model already knows the scene family, planning may be exploiting visual familiarity rather than action generalization.
papers.adversarial: Pose-image conditioning can hide dynamics, contact, and force; imagined rollouts need physical violation checks.
papers.thinking_tool: Separate plan proposal quality from world-model rollout fidelity and search contribution under equal compute.
papers.transfer_boundary: Transfers to compositional robot tasks with renderable embodiment state; harder when robot-environment contact is under-modeled.

papers.title: ODEWorld: A Continuous Predictive Architecture via Physical-Time Flow
papers.fit: physical-time flow - continuous world model - policy learning
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Discrete next-step latent predictors can produce jagged or collapsed trajectories that do not reflect smooth physical evolution.
papers.friction: A useful world model for policies should predict over physical time while remaining fast enough for planning and policy learning.
papers.hidden_premise: Decoupled dynamical representations and first-order supervision can make latent trajectories smoother and more useful for control.
papers.conceptual_move: ODEWorld models latent dynamics through physical-time flow, then uses the representation for video prediction and policy learning.
papers.mechanism: A PT-Flow representation evolves compressed visual features through a continuous dynamics model, with ablations on representation decoupling and first-order supervision.

evidence.claim: The paper visualizes smoother latent trajectories for ODEWorld than DINO features or a next-step predictive baseline.
Short-fragment prediction reports PSNR 20.53, LPIPS 0.109, and latency 0.030s for ODEWorld in the shown table.
The official HTML states that ODEWorld improves policy performance on LIBERO-LONG.
The appendix lists ablations on dynamical representation decoupling, first-order supervision, vision encoders, and token numbers.

papers.falsification: If smoother latent trajectories do not improve intervention planning or contact-sensitive policy learning, physical-time flow is mostly representation aesthetics.
papers.adversarial: Video metrics and smoothness can reward over-regularized dynamics that underfit abrupt contact or discontinuous object events.
papers.thinking_tool: Pair every world-model smoothness metric with action success, contact failure, and rollout divergence.
papers.transfer_boundary: Good for continuous visual dynamics and policy pretraining; needs contact-aware state for manipulation with discontinuities.

papers.title: LabEvolver: Training-Free Experience Evolution for Safe and Grounded Wet-Lab Agents
papers.fit: wet-lab agent - episodic experience evolution - safety gate
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Lab agents often correct within a trial but fail to distill completed experience into reusable skills, strategies, and safety rules.
papers.friction: Scientific automation needs online perception, planning, and safety validation while also preventing memory from growing into raw trace clutter.
papers.hidden_premise: Completed trajectories can be compressed into reusable experience without updating model weights.
papers.conceptual_move: LabEvolver uses an inner state-grounded trial loop and an outer experience-evolution loop for training-free wet-lab agents.
papers.mechanism: An Observer tracks hierarchical lab state, an Operator maps goals to LabSkill actions under a tri-layer safety gate, and a Strategist distills completed traces.

evidence.claim: The overview shows LabEvolver improving pH regulation through accumulated experience beyond one-shot or within-trial correction.
The dual-loop framework separates inner trial execution from outer strategy, skill, and safety experience evolution.
The HTML reports reduced MAE and execution time compared with PD controller baselines in pouring.
The paper reports pH-regulation completion time and safety-gate intercept reductions of 48.2% and 60.0%, and ALFWorld success from 76.2% to 91.4%.

papers.falsification: If distilled experience fails under a new reagent, vessel, or safety constraint, the memory may be task replay rather than grounded scientific abstraction.
papers.adversarial: Training-free does not mean risk-free; safety gates must be audited for false negatives, not only fewer intercepts.
papers.thinking_tool: Summarize an agent trace into skill, strategy, safety rule, evidence source, and stop condition before adding it to memory.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for procedural lab tasks with measurable state; less direct for open-world manipulation without stable skill APIs.

papers.title: Articulated Object Reconstruction from Rest-State Observation
papers.fit: articulated reconstruction - rest-state inference - kinematic digital twin
papers.status: Tier A - official arXiv HTML verified
papers.status_quo: Articulated-object reconstruction usually assumes multiple observed articulation states or visible motion.
papers.friction: Robots often see a closed cabinet or drawer before interaction and still need to infer parts and joints.
papers.hidden_premise: Geometry, semantics, and motion priors can compensate for missing motion cues if cross-model verification is explicit.
papers.conceptual_move: The paper reconstructs articulated objects from a single rest-state observation using mesh intermediates, VLM/segmentation evidence, and diffusion-generated articulation hypotheses.
papers.mechanism: Noisy part hierarchies and masks are fused into spatially consistent structures; synthesized articulation videos support joint-parameter estimation without observed motion.

evidence.claim: The method reconstructs part-level geometry and joint parameters from rest-state observations alone.
The paper shows naive pretrained VLM, segmentation, and video-diffusion failures on a closed cabinet example.
The comparison table positions the method against articulated reconstruction methods requiring multiple states or part-count priors.
The HTML lists part segmentation, joint estimation, ablation, and diverse-input generalization evaluations.

papers.falsification: If synthesized articulation hypotheses are plausible but wrong, a robot can plan an invalid interaction with high confidence.
papers.adversarial: Rest-state priors are powerful but can hallucinate affordances; physical probing or uncertainty is needed before execution.
papers.thinking_tool: For object reconstruction, log which joint came from observation, segmentation, VLM prior, diffusion hypothesis, or physical probe.
papers.transfer_boundary: Strong for cabinets, drawers, and structured objects; weaker for deformable or broken mechanisms without strong priors.

synthesis.title: S1 - Counterfactual coverage is replacing demo count
synthesis.links: Counterfactual Action Sensitivity Coverage - RedFlow - ACE-Data-0
synthesis.facts: CFNBC selects nuisance examples by action drift, RedFlow turns failed actions into corrective targets, and ACE captures synchronized interaction state.
synthesis.inference: The relevant unit of data is no longer a demonstration; it is a state-action contrast that changes a policy or explains a failure.
synthesis.decision: APRL should rank new data by action sensitivity, correction value, and preserved physical channel.

synthesis.title: S2 - World-action models are filling missing state channels
synthesis.links: EgoGenesis - TacWAM - World Action Planner - ODEWorld
synthesis.facts: The papers add anchored 3D memory, tactile mechanics, pose-image rollouts, and physical-time flow to world-action modeling.
synthesis.inference: A future is useful when it preserves the variable needed by the planner or controller, not when it is merely coherent.
synthesis.decision: APRL should evaluate WAMs with channel-specific state probes and downstream repair tests.

synthesis.title: S3 - Agents need reusable experience summaries with safety fields
synthesis.facts: LabEvolver distills experience into skill, strategy, and safety memories; RedFlow localizes correction; TacWAM blocks future tactile leakage into action.
synthesis.inference: Experience reuse is defensible only when the state, safety rule, and information boundary are explicit.
synthesis.decision: APRL should make memory entries include evidence source, allowed use, safety gate, and stop condition.

synthesis.title: S4 - Geometry becomes a prior that must declare uncertainty
synthesis.links: Rest-state articulated reconstruction - EgoGenesis - World Action Planner
synthesis.facts: Rest-state reconstruction infers hidden joints, EgoGenesis anchors 3D scene memory, and World Action Planner renders robot pose into world-model rollouts.
synthesis.inference: Geometry is moving into the action loop, so hallucinated structure becomes an execution risk rather than a visualization error.
synthesis.decision: APRL should require uncertainty and source tags for geometry used in planning.

frontier_memory.title: Action-sensitive data is now a repeated robotics axis
frontier_memory.history: Earlier July releases emphasized rollout ledgers, causal modality effects, and execution-time verification.
frontier_memory.read: July 31 adds counterfactual action drift and failure-to-correction targets as concrete data-selection mechanisms.

frontier_memory.title: World-action models are becoming multi-channel state models
frontier_memory.history: Recent WAM papers moved from video prediction to dynamic tokens, 3D object priors, and action-conditioned verification.
frontier_memory.read: EgoGenesis, TacWAM, ODEWorld, and World Action Planner add 3D memory, tactile mechanics, physical time, and pose-image action state.

frontier_memory.title: Ambient capture and wet-lab experience are converging as data engines
frontier_memory.history: Prior data discussions focused on robot demonstrations, simulation, or resettable benchmarks.
frontier_memory.read: ACE and LabEvolver make synchronized human-state capture and distilled lab experience look like reusable infrastructure.

frontier_memory.title: Most world-model papers still need failure-conditioned channel ablations
frontier_memory.history: Many papers add state channels and report aggregate improvements.
frontier_memory.read: The missing audit is which channel predicts or repairs which failure family under equal compute and data budgets.

strategy.title: Counterfactual Action-Sensitivity Data Engine
strategy.thesis: Select and generate robot data by the action drift or correction it induces, not by raw demonstration count.
strategy.one_week: Take one existing imitation policy and generate nuisance pairs for lighting, distractor, object pose, and moving-object state; measure action drift.
strategy.four_week: Add RedFlow-style corrective target matching and compare random demos, action-drift examples, and failure-correction examples under the same budget.
strategy.metric: OOD success +10p at equal data budget, with at least one selected example family explaining a specific failure mode.
strategy.stop: If action-drift examples do not outperform random additions on two nuisance families, narrow the generator or switch to real perturbation collection.

strategy.title: Multi-Channel World-Action Model Audit
strategy.thesis: Test which missing physical channel makes a WAM useful: 3D memory, tactile mechanics, pose-image rollout, or physical-time flow.
strategy.one_week: Define four channel probes on one manipulation task: visual-only, anchored 3D memory, tactile future, and pose-conditioned rollout.
strategy.four_week: Train or adapt small WAM variants and measure channel ablation, plan success, contact failure, repair lead time, and compute.
strategy.metric: A channel-specific probe predicts or repairs its target failure family with AUC >= 0.75 or success +10p.
strategy.stop: If no channel beats a visual-only WAM under equal compute, convert the result into a negative benchmark note.

strategy.title: Reusable Experience Memory With Safety Fields
strategy.thesis: Convert agent traces into compact, typed experience cards: skill, strategy, state evidence, safety gate, and stop condition.
strategy.one_week: Summarize five APRL lab or robot traces into experience cards and label which field would have changed the next attempt.
strategy.four_week: Integrate the cards into a small planning loop and compare raw trace retrieval, card retrieval, and no memory.
strategy.metric: Card retrieval improves success or reduces safety interrupts while keeping memory size bounded.
strategy.stop: If cards do not outperform raw trace retrieval or introduce unsafe reuse, keep them as human-facing documentation only.
